one_line_contribution: A pre-registered ALFWorld measurement of the residual value of a procedural memory bank once a reflective prompt optimizer (GEPA-lite) has written an instruction from the identical training episodes, with an episode-disjoint, no-memory-accuracy-matched instruction as the control that is meant to separate 'the instruction absorbed these episodes' from 'the instruction learned this distribution'. The proposal is honest that the qualitative result is already published and that the contribution is an interval plus an identification arm on top of it; I can state the contribution, but it is a measurement, not a claim.
closest_prior_work: ExpeL (arXiv 2308.10144), which the proposal concedes. I verified the paper exists and that its ALFWorld ablation does compare full / retrieve-only / insights-only and concludes the two containers are 'essential and synergistic' with retrieval mattering more on ALFWorld; the specific 59/55/50 numbers were not visible in the returned snippets, so the load-bearing framing number is unverified from this node. ExpeL threatens novelty because it already establishes container redundancy on the same benchmark from one training pool, and 85-93% single-container recovery is close enough to 'residual is small' that a reviewer will ask what the interval buys. It does NOT fully threaten, because ExpeL's insight block is a fixed extraction routine at a fixed retrieval budget, not a search-based optimizer with per-instruction re-tuned k, and ExpeL has no episode-disjoint level-matched arm. EvoAgentBench (arXiv 2607.05202) is the second threat and is the weaker concession than the proposal implies: the ID exists, but the returned abstract describes web research, algorithmic reasoning, software engineering and knowledge work via Ability Graphs, with no ALFWorld and no confirmation of the '528/267 trajectories on Qwen3.5-27B, ReasoningBank +3.6, GEPA +1.2' table the proposal quotes. So the claim 'an optimizer given the same episodes gets roughly what a bank gets is also published' is currently an out-of-domain extrapolation the proposal presents as settled.
strongest_objection: The confirmatory family is arithmetically unlikely to ever fire, and every pre-registered fallback lands on a restatement of ExpeL. By the proposal's own numbers, E (equivalence within +/-3pt) is declarable only when |g-hat(I_P)| <= 0.9pt, and D is powered at ~4pt while thresholded at 3pt, so the intersection E AND D that licenses the title has low probability even under the authors' own planning assumptions; the modal outcome is a 'bounded residual' in (0.9, 3] plus 'distribution-level absorption', i.e. 37,600 episodes to say what ExpeL's ablation table already says qualitatively. Compounding this, D is confounded in a way no arm removes: I'_match is an EARLY SNAPSHOT (r in {50,100,200,350,500}) of a longer run, matched to I_P only on no-memory S_dev accuracy. Matching accuracy does not match optimization degree or instruction specificity, so g(I'_match) > g(I_P) is equally well explained by 'I_P is a converged, densely specified instruction that crowds the context and I' is an undercooked one' as by 'I_P absorbed these particular episodes'. Row 6 (I0_pad) controls length but not specificity, and the row-3/row-2 contrast is the paper's only identification. Two further defects make the primaries fragile at the 3pt scale they are decided at: (i) row 9 is labelled the treatment-free null replicate but it is I_P x {M0, B} at seed 37, which is the SAME treatment contrast at a different decoding seed, so pooling it into the 'null floor' contaminates the null with the real effect and makes the 95th-percentile floor rise exactly when memory works; (ii) k*(I) is chosen per instruction by maximizing paired gain over k in {1,3,5,7} at 75 games per k, where the SE of a paired gain is roughly 5-6pt, so the 'bank's own re-tuned retrieval budget' - contribution (ii) in the Related Work - is selected essentially at random, and independent noisy k-selections for I_P and I'_match feed straight into D's 3pt threshold. The agent-model and bank-format screening is worse: a 5pt threshold judged on 50 games picks the whole downstream stack on noise, and G1's subsequent 5pt requirement is then evaluated on the winner of that selection.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Fix the null: make row 9 a genuine treatment-free replicate (I_P x M0 at two decoding seeds, and B x B at two seeds), and stop pooling a live treatment contrast into the null floor. 2) Fix the power problem rather than pre-registering around it: the reserve (~700 trials) should go into rows 2-3 up front, and the margin should be set from the measured S_dev SE, not planned at +/-3pt when the design can only declare 0.9pt; alternatively drop TOST and make the retention ratio R = g(I_P)/g(I0*) with a CI the PRIMARY endpoint, which is estimable at this n and is the quantity practitioners actually want. 3) De-confound D: match I'_match to I_P on optimizer budget AND on instruction token count and rule count, not only on no-memory accuracy, and add the symmetric arm - I_P evaluated against B' vs B is row 4, but the missing mirror is I'_match x B' (its own-episode bank), which turns a one-sided comparison into a 2x2 provenance design where the interaction, not a difference of differences across unmatched instructions, is the estimand. 4) Move k*(I) selection to a sample size where it means something (all 300 S_dev games per k, or a single shared k with the k-curve reported as the sensitivity analysis), or pre-register k as fixed and report re-tuning as secondary. 5) Add an upper-bound memory arm (gold trajectory of the exact test task injected at I_P) so that g(I_P) ~ 0 can be distinguished from 'the I_P prompt does not read the memory slot at all'; the item-following rate f(I) is an action-string heuristic that any accuracy change perturbs and cannot carry that load alone. 6) Verify and quote EvoAgentBench's actual table, or drop it as a concession; the argument currently leans on an out-of-domain benchmark whose numbers were not readable from this node.
missing_baseline: The static demonstration container from the same episodes, at Tier 0. The paper's claim is 'the bank is worth nothing once the instruction has seen these episodes', but the only memory-slot contents in the Tier-0 grid are the retrieved bank B, its provenance variants (B', B^on) and a random-item control. A reviewer will demand I_P x C (the token-matched compiled block from B) and a MIPROv2-style bootstrapped k-shot demonstration set drawn from P_train with the retriever removed - both currently relegated to Tier 1. Without them the design cannot separate 'retrieval adds nothing over an optimized instruction' from 'this particular distilled bank adds nothing', which is the difference between a claim about memory systems and a claim about one bank. Second omission, and the one the research-track brief actually asks for: the coupling arm I2 (instruction optimized WITH the bank in context) x {B, M0} is the deployment configuration every framework in the related work ships, and it is also Tier 1; a proposal titled around whether memory is an un-optimized prompt that never runs the co-optimized condition in its main grid has skipped the composition the track posed. Third: no bank-size scaling arm (B at 150/300/600 episodes), so a null residual at 300 episodes cannot be distinguished from a bank that is simply too small.
preprint_collision: The check is unusually candid - it names its own conceded collisions and lists four unrun obligations - but it is by its own admission incomplete, and obligation (1), the provenance / held-out-episode crossover search, is the one the author states would reduce the contribution to 'the ALFWorld measurement with its controls'. One query run and nothing found is not a search. Under this venue's standard that is a weakness, not a neutral. My own six searches: VERIFIED EXISTS AND SAYS WHAT THE PROPOSAL SAYS - arXiv 2604.14585 'Prompt Optimization Is a Coin Flip: Diagnosing When It Helps in Compound AI Systems' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.14585), 72 runs, 49% below zero-shot on Claude Haiku, ICML 2026 workshop; arXiv 2507.19457 GEPA, confirmed ICLR 2026 Oral; arXiv 2308.10144 ExpeL, ALFWorld full vs retrieve-only vs insights-only ablation confirmed qualitatively, exact 59/55/50 values NOT confirmed in returned snippets; arXiv 2607.28272 'MemHarness: Memory Is Reconstructed, Not Replayed' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28272) exists, ALFWorld + WebShop, headline 85.2% ALFWorld, the quoted 70.1 vs 76.4 baseline pair not visible in snippets. PARTIALLY VERIFIED - arXiv 2607.05202 EvoAgentBench exists (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05202) but the returned abstract covers web research, algorithmic reasoning, software engineering and knowledge work via Ability Graphs, with no ALFWorld and no sign of the ReasoningBank +3.6 / GEPA +1.2 / 528-267 / Qwen3.5-27B table the proposal quotes as its central 'already published' concession. NO DIRECT COLLISION FOUND: two collision-targeted searches returned nothing that measures a memory bank's residual value at a search-optimized instruction built from the same episodes, and nothing with an episode-disjoint level-matched instruction control. NEAR MISSES THE CHECK DOES NOT LIST, all surfaced by my searches and all 2026: arXiv 2603.21520 'Generalizable Self-Evolving Memory for Automatic Prompt Optimization' (MemAPO), which reconceptualizes prompt optimization itself as accumulated experience with a dual success/error memory - this is the strongest unlisted adjacency, because it directly asserts the containers are the same object, and if its evaluation includes an instruction-vs-memory decomposition it collides with the framing if not the number; arXiv 2606.03083 DeltaMem, which stores experience as residual deltas to cut cross-episode redundancy and reports leading both ALFWorld splits with per-component ablations; arXiv 2603.12631 'Joint Optimization of Multi-agent Memory System'; arXiv 2608.04761 InsightEmb. None of these is a kill, so I did not move novelty down for a collision - but I did not move it up either, because the surviving contribution as stated ('an interval on top of an accepted qualitative result') is small, the author agrees it is small, and the unrun obligation (1) could still shrink it further. Anything I believe about pre-2026 memory-as-instruction work beyond these results is from my own memory and unverified.
